kind.text:
title: "A split pane driven to zero height, and the NSSplitView autosave that makes it permanent"
date: 2026-09-07
last_updated: 2026-10-14
category: ui-bugs
module: RcGitApp
problem_type: ui_bug
component: frontend
symptoms:
  - "A pane of a split renders at zero height; the feature in it reads as deleted, with no divider left to drag it back open"
  - "History tab shows only the search bar and the 'Select a commit' placeholder, no commit rows (2026-09-07 instance)"
  - "Clicking a changed file in the commit-detail drawer flashes 'Loading <path>…' and then renders nothing (2026-09-21 and 2026-09-25 instances)"
  - "A min/max coordinate clamp is in place and the pane is still at zero: those delegate methods bound a divider drag, nothing else"
  - "A pane has an Auto Layout height floor and still reaches zero: the split's delegate implements a sizing method, so the split places its panes by frame"
  - "The CLI returns the same data the view is asking for, so the core, FFI, and model layers are fine"
  - "A build with the layout fix still shows the broken pane: autosaveName restores the position the buggy build saved"
root_cause: logic_error
resolution_type: code_fix
severity: high
framework_version: macos 26.6.2
related_components: [appkit, autolayout, nssplitview, nssplitviewdelegate, userdefaults]
tags:
  [
    appkit,
    nssplitview,
    nssplitviewdelegate,
    autosavename,
    divider-position,
    zero-height,
    autolayout,
    nsstackview,
  ]

The drawer's changed-files list rendered fine and the diff pane below it was zero points tall. No broken constraint at all this time — just one pane with a min-height floor and one without.

The pane renders empty with no draggable divider to recover it. Instance 1: no commit rows, only the search bar and the "Select a commit" placeholder. Instance 2: clicking a changed file flashes "Loading
…" and then shows nothing — no diff, no error, no empty-diff message.
The CLI returns the data for the same input, pinning the bug to the view:
The stored geometry is itself degenerate. Reading it takes one command and no app launch:

$ defaults read com.timeturnback.rcgit.dev \
    "NSSplitView Subview Frames rc-git.history-detail.v3"
(
    "0.000000, 0.000000, 349.000000, 864.000000, NO, NO",
    "0.000000, 101.000000, 349.000000, 0.000000, YES, NO"
)

Trusting an Auto Layout floor to undo a restored position.

Floors on the panes of a split whose delegate sizes it (instance 3).
Stronger than the point above: there the floor does not govern the
layout either. A split with arranged subviews and no sizing delegate methods sizes its panes with Auto Layout, and a pane floor holds. Implementing

This was instance 2's "durable part". It is not durable: AppKit asks those methods where a divider the user is

recorded a diff pane at zero height — and their mere presence switched the split to frame mode, which is what disabled the pane floors. Keep them only on a split whose layout the delegate already owns; do not count them as the guard.

1. Hide a view by detaching it, never by collapsing its height.

2. Floor the split, not its panes, and keep the floors in
The two heights are thresholds, so they live where the repo's invariant says thresholds live —

The coordinate clamps bound a drag, and only on the two splits whose layout the controller already owns, so implementing them costs nothing that frame mode had not already given up:

Step 3 repairs a poisoned key on its own, so the bump is only about the first launch after the fix: at instance 3, without it the repaired position was the old one clamped — a 613pt file list above a 150pt diff — instead of the 100pt list and full-height diff a fresh key gave.

Auto Layout cannot satisfy both, so AppKit picked constraints to break — and it does not pick predictably. Here it sacrificed the constraints keeping the commits pane open, and the enclosing split collapsed it to zero.

Instance 2 needed neither of those. With a floor on one pane and none on the other, the split had a perfectly legal layout in which the file list took its 100pt minimum and the diff took everything left — including nothing. The drawer laid out at least once with nothing to spare, the divider went to the bottom, and the diff pane went to zero. No constraint was broken; the layout was simply unconstrained in the direction that hurt.
In both, the same second stage made it permanent:
wrote that position to user defaults under its
Autosave is a recorder, not a validator.
It captures whatever geometry exists, sane or not, and re-imposes it on the next launch — which is why the constraint fix alone changed nothing on the user's machine.
Instance 3 is what happens when the fix addresses neither stage. An
runs in one of two modes. With arranged subviews and a delegate that implements no sizing method, it sizes its panes with Auto Layout: the panes keep
off and a pane floor holds. A delegate that implements
switches it to frame mode: it assigns each pane a frame, turns
on, and that frame becomes required constraints. A

alongside is then the weaker half of a contradiction, and AppKit breaks it without a word. A headless probe shows the switch: a split with no sizing delegate methods kept a floored pane at 150pt, and the same split with a delegate implementing only an identity

on. Apple's reference for each of those four methods says not to implement it when a split uses Auto Layout. Instance 2 implemented both clamps in the commit that added the floors, so the floors never governed the computed layout. And the coordinate clamps never saw the restore: AppKit asks those methods where a divider
does not consult them, and neither does the autosave, which restores by setting frames. Both mechanisms were present and correct in the
build, and neither was ever on the path that produced
puts the policy on the one path every resize takes, and

covers the restore, which reaches the screen through a layout pass rather than a resize. Between them there is no way for the split to display a geometry the policy did not produce — which is the property the earlier fixes only appeared to have.
The version bump is the weakest of the four. Renaming
orphans a poisoned key; it never repairs one, and it only buys one clean launch.

— the fix for that — was poisoned the same way. A name bump is a reset button. The layout the app owns is the guard, and it is the first version of this fix that also
a key instead of abandoning it.
In instance 2 the "Loading…" flash was visible only by accident of where the placeholder lives:
is centered in the drawer's container, not inside the diff scroll view, so it drew across the whole drawer while
a moment later wrote real hunks into a view with no pixels. The user saw the loading state and never the result.
Never collapse a view with a height-0 constraint while it has visible subviews.
The subviews' compression resistance makes the system unsatisfiable and AppKit breaks constraints arbitrarily — often far from the offending view. Put the view in an
; a detached view costs no height and fights nothing.
Pick one mode per split and never mix them.
Either keep the delegate out of sizing (implement none of
) and floor the panes with Auto Layout, plus
, place both panes from one pure function in
, and put the minimum on the split itself, as both History splits do now. Apple's reference says not to implement those methods on a split that uses Auto Layout.
Adding any clamp to an Auto Layout split is the change that broke instance 3.
is enough to flip the split to frame mode and silently disable every pane floor. On a split in frame mode a pane constraint is not a floor: the split assigns pane frames and
bound a drag and nothing else.
, not the autosave restore. Implement them only on a split whose layout the delegate already owns, and never count them as the guard. An
sets it on both items of

Whether History's left column should move back to Auto Layout mode is a separate code decision: measure the autosave restore in that mode before relying on it.
Re-audit whenever a pane is added or a split is restructured.
A restructure flips which axis is at risk, which is the whole story of

: it flipped both splits' orientation at once, correctly swapping the commits pane's height floor for a width one, and leaving the diff pane unprotected on the height axis it had just started bearing. Neither pane was new; the geometry was.

separates "code bug" from "poisoned user defaults" instantly, with no app launch — which matters because the working agreement forbids launching the app to verify. Check both bundle ids:
